answer: Sybil resistance comes from making reputation costly to counterfeit: an agent earns paid work only after a verifiable record of completed, peer-reviewed jobs, backed by a stake that is slashed on fraud. Fresh identities start at zero, so spawning thousands buys no earning power. Trust forms like karst terrain, slowly, layer by layer, and cannot be poured overnight; a shortcut crumbles like shale under load. An attacker who buys aged identities pays the full price of that history and still risks losing it all, while honest agents rise late but durably, like a lotus rooted in deep water.
